change.describe: branch `pr-80329-flat` of grafana-80329-flat against a886bd3c79a417a70b51509384d1f1ec3e87e96b (merge-base a886bd3)
change.title: pr-80329-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Quadratic string building for the SQLite inline ID list
findings.body: The SQLite inline branch builds the ID list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop, so each iteration copies the whole accumulated string. For a 32767-ID batch (the case cleanup_test.go:98-111 exercises) that is about n^2/2 x ~7 bytes, roughly 3.7 GB of copying per batch, repeated for every batch of every cleanup cycle. Build the list with strings.Builder or strings.Join over strconv.FormatInt(v, 10).
findings.originReason: deleteByIDs and its inline SQLite branch are new in this diff.

verification.reason: Line 611 rebuilds the whole accumulated string with fmt.Sprintf on every iteration, so building the list is O(n²) and runs on every batch. The test at cleanup_test.go:98-111 uses a 32767 batch. This branch only runs on SQLite with a non-default batch size above 999 (the default is 100, setting.go:710), so one step lower is the better severity.

findings.title: Successful cleanup progress is logged at Error level with the full ID list
findings.body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579 log every batch at Error level, and 534/554/576 include the whole `ids` slice. Default batch size is 100 (pkg/setting/setting.go:710) and the job now runs every minute (pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77), so a healthy instance writes several ERROR lines per minute even when nothing failed. At lines 534, 554 and 576 the `"err"` field is always nil because the error check just above has returned. Use Debug (or Info for the per-run summary) and drop the ID list from the message.
findings.originReason: These log calls were added in this diff.

verification.reason: Every batch logs at Error level, including the final empty batch that ends the loop. Lines 534, 554 and 576 include the full ids slice and an err that is always nil, because the error check just above has already returned. With the new 1-minute ticker, any instance with cleanup enabled writes ERROR lines every minute even when nothing fails.

findings.title: Unbounded placeholder count on MySQL/Postgres for large batch sizes
findings.body: deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID on every dialect except SQLite-with-batch>999. The batch size is user-configurable with no upper bound (pkg/setting/setting.go:710 is a plain MustInt64(100)). The previous code inlined LIMIT as a literal, so a configured batch above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535 for Postgres and for MySQL prepared statements, from driver knowledge not checked in this repo) worked before and now fails on every run once that many rows match. The error is returned from CleanAnnotations, so Run (pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup.go:37-41) stops at the first type and the other annotation types and the orphan-tag pass are skipped every cycle. Either clamp the batch size used for placeholders to a safe maximum, or use the inline form for every dialect as the SQLite branch does (with proper escaping of the integer IDs, which are safe).
findings.originReason: The base ran a single DELETE with a subquery and no bound parameters; per-ID placeholders are new.

verification.reason: Outside the SQLite-above-999 case, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID (lines 615-617), and the batch size has no upper bound (setting.go:710). A batch above the driver's parameter limit therefore fails, and Run returns at the first type (cleanup.go:37-41), skipping the remaining types and the orphan-tag pass. The base inlined LIMIT as a literal and bound no parameters. It only triggers with an unusually large configured batch, so severity is one step lower.

findings.title: MaxCount delete can remove a row that is now among the newest N
findings.body: The MaxCount path fetches IDs by rank (`ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT n OFFSET maxCount`, lines 549-553) and then deletes those IDs by primary key without re-checking rank (line 556). The old single statement re-evaluated the subquery atomically. If a newer annotation is deleted between the fetch and the delete (for example through the Delete API), a row that was at rank maxCount is now inside the keep set, but it is still deleted. The comment at lines 524-525 only documents under-deletion, not this over-deletion of a user's annotation. The window is one batch round-trip, so this is rare, but the loss is silent. The MaxAge path is not affected because `created` is never updated (the update column list at pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:182 excludes it).
findings.originReason: The split into fetch and delete replaced the base's single atomic DELETE ... WHERE id IN (subquery).

verification.reason: The MaxCount path fetches IDs by rank (line 549) and then deletes them by primary key (line 556) without re-checking rank. If a top-N row is deleted in between, the row at the boundary is deleted even though it is now inside the keep set. The window is one round-trip, and the lost row would be pushed out by the next insert anyway, so consider is the better severity.

findings.title: Ticker change makes every cleanup job run 10x as often
findings.body: The ticker goes from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which applies to all jobs in clean() (pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:96-105), not only annotation cleanup. That includes query-history enforcement (lines 266 and 275), snapshot, dashboard-version, image and invite expiry, and temp-file scans. The job also logs "Completed cleanup jobs" at Info on every run (line 120). The PR body says 'Database Performance Optimizations' and does not mention this change, while it multiplies background DB load by 10. Is one-minute cadence intended for every job? If not, restore the 10-minute interval; if it is, state the reason in the PR body and confirm the per-minute query-history limit enforcement is acceptable.
findings.originReason: This diff changed time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1.

verification.reason: The ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. It drives clean(), which runs every job in the list (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history), and line 120 logs at Info on every run.

findings.title: 'running the max count delete again' no longer runs the delete twice
findings.body: Each subtest now resets the tables (cleanup at lines 120-127) and creates its own fixture. This subtest creates 9 annotations (3 per type) and runs MaxCount=3 once, so it only checks that nothing is deleted from an already-trimmed set. The previous version ran after 'should only keep three annotations' had left the table trimmed, so the name described a second run. Either run the cleanup twice inside this subtest, or rename it to reflect what it checks.
findings.originReason: Before this diff the subtests shared one fixture created once at line 28, so this subtest ran a second delete on already-trimmed data.

verification.reason: Each subtest now creates its own fixture (line 116) and wipes the tables in cleanup (lines 120-127). This subtest creates 9 annotations, 3 per type (i%3 distribution), and runs MaxCount=3 once, so it never runs the delete a second time. In the base it ran after the previous subtest on shared data.

contracts.action: Background MaxAge annotation cleanup: fetch IDs by age, then delete them by ID in batches
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed executeUntilDoneOrCancelled with one DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... LIMIT) per batch (previous version of CleanAnnotations)
contracts.before_after: Before: one autocommit DELETE per batch, the subquery evaluated in the database. After: a SELECT id ... LIMIT (fetchIDs) followed by DELETE ... WHERE id IN (ids) (deleteByIDs), two statements per batch, plus two Error log lines per batch.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. ERROR-level log lines per batch, including the ID list (xorm_store.go:534, 537).
contracts.failure_mode: A fetch or delete error is returned from untilDoneOrCancelled and CleanAnnotations, so Run returns early (pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup.go:39-41). cleanUpOldAnnotations logs the error (pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:126-127). The remaining annotation types and the orphan-tag pass are skipped for that cycle and retried on the next tick. Nothing is left half-done, because each batch is either fully fetched and deleted or not.

contracts.action: Background MaxCount annotation cleanup: fetch IDs by rank (ORDER BY id DESC OFFSET maxCount), delete them by ID
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT OFFSET) with executeUntilDoneOrCancelled
contracts.before_after: Before: the rank predicate was evaluated atomically inside the DELETE statement. After: the rank is evaluated in the SELECT, and the DELETE only checks the IDs, so the decision and the action are separate statements.
contracts.visible_effect: If a top-N annotation is deleted concurrently, a row that should be kept can be removed (see finding at line 556). The same error logs as the MaxAge path.
contracts.failure_mode: A concurrent Delete between fetch and delete removes a row the user meant to keep. No error is shown and no log records it.

contracts.action: Orphaned annotation_tag cleanup: fetch IDs of tags with no annotation, delete by ID
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed DELETE FROM annotation_tag WHERE id IN (SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS ... LIMIT) via executeUntilDoneOrCancelled
contracts.before_after: Same predicate and batch limit as before, split into a SELECT and a DELETE by ID per batch.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. Error-level logs per batch (xorm_store.go:576, 579).
contracts.failure_mode: A failure is returned to Run (cleanup.go:54-57) and then to cleanUpOldAnnotations, which logs it. The orphan pass runs only when totalCleanedAnnotations > 0 (cleanup.go:54), so if an earlier type fails after deleting annotations, the tags left behind are only retried on a later run that deletes something. This ordering predates the change.

contracts.action: DELETE of annotation / annotation_tag rows by a list of IDs, on every dialect
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/dashboardversion/dashverimpl/xorm_store.go:58-72 DeleteBatch: same fetch-then-delete-by-ID with a generated IN (?,?...) list and no re-check of the predicate
contracts.before_after: Before: the statement carried its own predicate and LIMIT. After: the statement carries only the IDs fetched earlier. Nothing re-checks the predicate between the fetch and the delete.
contracts.visible_effect: Rows fetched earlier are deleted even if they stopped matching the predicate in between (see the MaxCount finding). For MaxAge the predicate is `created < cutoff` plus alert_id type, and neither column is updated by the Update path (xorm_store.go:182), so there is no over-deletion on that path.
contracts.failure_mode: If Exec fails, the error is returned and the batch is dropped. The next tick re-fetches, so no record is orphaned by this step. Nothing outside the listed IDs is touched.

contracts.action: Placeholder form of the ID delete for MySQL, Postgres and SQLite with batch size <= 999
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous inline LIMIT form (no bind parameters, so no parameter-count limit)
contracts.before_after: Before: no bind parameters at all, because the batch size was a literal in the SQL. After: one bind parameter per fetched ID, so the count is bounded by the driver's parameter limit.
contracts.visible_effect: A configured batch size above the driver's bind-parameter limit makes the cleanup fail on every run once enough rows match. Annotations stop being cleaned and the error is logged.
contracts.failure_mode: Error returned up the call chain as described in the MaxAge contract. The cleanup stops for all types on every cycle, so annotation growth is not bounded.
contracts.open_question: What is the bind-parameter limit of the MySQL and Postgres drivers this repo uses? If it is 65535, a configured cleanupjob_batchsize above that fails. Confirm from the driver version in go.mod and from the driver source.

contracts.action: New call: session.SQL(sql).Find(&ids) into []int64 in fetchIDs
contracts.before_after: Same pattern: raw SQL, Find into a slice of int64, error returned directly. The new code runs in its own WithDbSession and does not share a transaction with the delete, as the sibling in dashverimpl does not either.
contracts.visible_effect: None directly; the IDs feed the delete.
contracts.failure_mode: An error returns (ids, err) and no delete runs. The caller returns the error (xorm_store.go:530-532, 550-552, 572-574). Nothing is lost.

contracts.action: New call: r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite in deleteByIDs
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/infra/serverlock/serverlock.go:245 and pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:122 compare GetDBType() with migrator constants
contracts.visible_effect: Chooses between inline IDs and placeholders for SQLite batches above 999.
contracts.failure_mode: None beyond the placeholder finding above.

contracts.action: Cleanup service ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
contracts.equivalent_path: The same loop with a 10-minute ticker (previous value of the line)
contracts.before_after: Before: clean() ran every 10 minutes. After: every minute. Each run executes all jobs in clean() (cleanup.go:96-105), including query-history enforcement and temp-file scans.
contracts.visible_effect: The Info line 'Completed cleanup jobs' (cleanup.go:120) is written every minute. Database load for every cleanup job is 10x what it was.
contracts.failure_mode: If a run takes longer than a minute, ticks are dropped and the next run starts at the next tick. clean() has a 9-minute context timeout (cleanup.go:89). Job errors are logged per job, so nothing is silent.

summary: Reviewed the three files of this part: xorm_store.go (the batched cleanup rewrite), cleanup_test.go (test restructuring) and cleanup.go (ticker change). The core approach (fetch IDs, delete by ID per batch, stop on zero affected) is sound and the MaxAge predicate is safe because `created` is never updated. Main problems: a quadratic string build for the SQLite inline ID list (xorm_store.go:611); success progress logged at Error level with full ID lists every batch (xorm_store.go:534 and siblings); placeholders for every dialect with no clamp on the user-configurable batch size, which can break cleanup above the driver's bind-parameter limit (open: driver limit not verified in repo); a MaxCount race where a concurrent delete of a top-N annotation lets a row that should be kept be deleted (xorm_store.go:556); the ticker change from 10 to 1 minute affects every cleanup job and is not described in the PR body (cleanup.go:77); and the 'running the max count delete again' subtest no longer runs a second delete (cleanup_test.go:83). Nothing was built or run.
